title: Advaita (Shankara): not-two; rope and snake in full; the Vivekachudamani opening (6 of 7)
hook: five sheaths, one inside another, and a sword that isn't any of them
tomorrow: Advaita (Shankara): not-two; rope and snake in full; the Vivekachudamani opening (7 of 7)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the student burning, and the teacher's first words. Don't be afraid; there is a way. Your line: not two. Did someone get comfort before answers? Today, the teacher starts showing the way. Day two hundred eighty-six.
screen: `DON'T BE AFRAID. THERE IS A WAY.`

segments.voice: An old sword lies in a museum case. It's sheathed in a leather scabbard, and the scabbard is wrapped in cloth, and the cloth is tied with cord, and the whole thing rests in a carved wooden box. From the outside, you see the box. You might even think the box is the treasure. But the sword is inside all of it, and it isn't the box or the cloth or the leather. Vedanta teachers use a Sanskrit word for layers like these, kosha, which can mean a sheath, a covering, a treasury. And they say you're wrapped in five of them.
screen: `A SWORD IN A MUSEUM CASE.` → `BOX, CORD, CLOTH, LEATHER.` → `FIVE SHEATHS.`

segments.voice: The list comes from the Taittiriya Upanishad, which calls them selves, one inside another, and the Vivekachudamani walks through it layer by layer. Outermost, the sheath made of food: the body. It's literally built from what you eat, and it goes back to food, to the earth, in the end. Inside it, the sheath of breath, the life force that keeps the body warm and moving. Inside that, the sheath of mind: the stream of thoughts, wants, and worries. Inside that, the sheath of understanding: the part that decides, judges, and says I'm the one doing this. And innermost, the sheath of bliss: the deep peace you touch in dreamless sleep, or in a moment of pure joy. Five coverings. And here is the Advaita move, neti neti one layer at a time. Each sheath is something you can notice. You notice the body. You notice the breath. You notice thoughts come and go. You notice yourself deciding. Even the bliss, you notice arriving and leaving. So none of them is the one noticing. Advaita teachers say the self shines through all five, the way the sun shines through colored glass without becoming colored. Not the box. Not the cloth. The sword. An honest note: Hindu schools read this passage differently. Shankara's school says even the bliss sheath is still a covering. Others, including Ramanuja's school, read the passage's bliss as pointing to Brahman itself. Same text, two readings. The next few days will say more about that difference.
screen: `FOOD, THE BODY.` · `BREATH, THEN MIND.` · `UNDERSTANDING, THEN BLISS.` · `THE ONE WHO NOTICES ALL FIVE.` · then, large: `NOT TWO.`

segments.voice: Sit, and move inward through the sheaths. The body: its weight and warmth. Noticed. The breath: in, out. Noticed. The mind: a thought, a plan, a worry. Noticed. Understanding: the part that says I'm doing this practice, am I doing it right? Noticed. Then, if a little peace shows up, that too: noticed. And rest as the one who noticed all five, for as long as it lasts. The bell holds the time.
Advaita, through the five sheaths: food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss. In Shankara's school, the self is none of them, but the awareness shining through all five.
Your line: not two. Today, when you eat, remember the sheath made of food, and notice: I'm feeding the body, and something is aware of it. Day two hundred eighty-six.

howItsDone: Many Vedanta and yoga teachers use the five koshas from the Taittiriya Upanishad as a map for contemplation, moving attention inward from the body through breath, mind and understanding to the bliss sheath, and in Advaita to the witness beyond them.

fork.setup: you notice your body, your breath, your thoughts, your decisions, even a moment of bliss. by the Vivekachudamani, which one are you?
options: none: you're what notices all five.
the mind: it's doing the noticing.
fork.reveal: each sheath can be noticed, so none is the noticer. the self shines through them, like sun through colored glass.

original.note: Sanskrit: pancha (five) + kosha (sheath, covering, treasury): the five sheaths.

trapdoor: what you thought: the self is the body, or maybe the mind.
what it means: the Upanishads list five sheaths, food, breath, mind, understanding, bliss; Advaita says the self is none of them.

what a scholar hears: Taittiriya Upanishad 2.1–5 names annamaya, prāṇamaya, manomaya, vijñānamaya and ānandamaya; Brahma Sutra 1.1.12 ff. is where Shankara and Ramanuja differ over whether the ānandamaya is Brahman.

sources.ref: Taittiriya Upanishad 2.1–5 (the five selves or sheaths)
Vivekachudamani (the section on the five sheaths)
Brahma Sutra 1.1.12–19 and the commentaries of Shankara and Ramanuja (the anandamaya)

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): hook opened with the banned 'Picture'; rewritten as a scene. The hook said 'the Upanishads use' the word kosha, but the Taittiriya calls the layers 'selves' (atman) and kosha is the later Vedanta term (as the existing note says); the hook and teach now say so.

Shankara's own Brahma Sutra commentary on 1.1.12 ff. is complex (he discusses and partly rejects an earlier reading); the script simplifies to 'Shankara's school says even the bliss sheath is still a covering'. Please check.
The colored-glass image is a common Advaita illustration; attributed in the script to Advaita teachers generally, not to the Vivekachudamani.
The Taittiriya calls these 'selves' (atman) made of food, breath, etc.; 'sheath' (kosha) is the later Vedanta term.
